subject: Re: QBR prep — product delivery flags & launch go/no-go
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 07 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: product delivery flags for upcoming launches

Team —

As we pull the material together for the QBR product readout, I want to surface current delivery flags that will materially affect the launch timelines and our Q2 OKR trajectory. Please review below and add owner-level updates inline by EOD Tuesday so I can consolidate a single slide for the exec readout. Attachments: release-readiness-checklist.pdf, launch-dependencies.csv.

Top-level flags (short):
- ProcureSync integration: third-party API to pull contract metadata is behind schedule; they indicated a potential 2-week slippage. Impact: blocks procurement flow for Dedicated customers (affects launch M1). Owner: Laura.
- GPU capacity for Dedicated: capacity reservations for the initial Dedicated pool are not yet confirmed in us-west. This could cause degraded throughput at launch. Impact: latency SLOs for launch cohort. Owner: Marissa.
- Quantization regression: Engineering found a minor but repeatable quality regression when applying the new 4-bit quantization profile to the customer-supplied Paraphrase model. Impact: customer-facing quality metric risk. Owner: Marissa.
- Docs & support playbooks: runbook incomplete for canary rollback steps and billing-side verification. Impact: operational risk during go-live. Owner: Ben.

Ask: please reply with: current status (green/amber/red), estimated delta to market date (days), mitigation steps, and confirmed owner. If any flag should be escalated to execs before the QBR, call it out explicitly.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
VP Product Operations
Redwood Inference

---
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: product delivery flags for upcoming launches

Thanks Markus — quick updates on the ProcureSync and timeline adjustments.

- ProcureSync integration (status: amber): Their API contract team ran into schema validation issues last week; they told us the earliest full-fidelity fix is ~10 business days. I asked for a partial response mode (metadata-only) that should recover ~80% of the flow; they're evaluating. Contingency: we can ship with ProcureSync in degraded mode and label it in the release notes. Estimated delta: 10–14 days to full feature parity, but launchable with limited functionality.
- Impact to OKRs: this affects the Dedicated-sales enablement OKR (reduce time-to-purchase by 20%). Recommend we split the OKR to reflect early-access intervals so we don't lose traction in the QBR metrics.

Action items I own:
- Drive ProcureSync partial contract by EOD Friday; coordinate with Legal to approve the limited-scope integration.
- Update launch slide to call out partial vs full capabilities and clearly state the customer impact.

Cc'ing Ben to confirm the docs playbook timing.

Laura Bennett
Head of Go-to-Market Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: product delivery flags for upcoming launches

Markus / team —

Engineering notes and mitigation for the two technical flags (GPU capacity and quantization regression).

1) GPU capacity (status: amber -> mitigation in progress):
- Root cause: delayed confirmation from cloud partner on reserved instance pool (us-west). We've raised it with partner ops; they have prioritized our request but can only guarantee allocation in 5 business days.
- Mitigation options:
  * Option A (preferred): Shift initial Dedicated lane to a hybrid pool that combines reserved nodes + burst-on-demand for the first 2 weeks. This preserves latency SLOs for 90% of traffic; requires a transient increase in unit costs.
  * Option B: Stagger the feature rollout by region (launch eu/us-west then expand), which keeps the overall launch date but delays some customers.
- Estimated delta: 3–7 business days to stabilize with Option A (cost delta to be quantified).

2) Quantization regression (status: amber -> working to green):
- Repro steps: 4-bit profile causes subtle tokenization differences for rare tokens in paraphrase testset, lowering BLEU-like metrics by ~2.5 points on our internal eval.
- Short-term mitigation: fallback to 8-bit profile for the affected model family during canary. Long-term: improve calibration layer and add targeted fine-tuning.
- Risk if unmitigated: customer-reported quality regressions that could impact NPS for the launch cohort.
- Owner: Marissa (engineering) and SRE for validation. ETA for full fix: 10 business days; ETA for safe fallback and automated QA gating: 3 days.

I am preparing a go/no-go matrix (attached draft to my internal note) and will circulate a CSV version for owners to mark final decisions. We should be able to present a conservative go recommendation for the execs if we commit to Option A for capacity and the 8-bit fallback for quant.

Marissa Cole
VP Engineering — Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR prep — product delivery flags & launch go/no-go

Team — thanks for the fast turn. Final consolidation and asks before I lock the QBR deck at EOD Friday.

Summary state:
- ProcureSync: amber; Laura to own partial-integration approval and slide language. Expect +10–14 days to full parity, but launchable with degraded mode.
- GPU capacity: amber; Marissa proposes Option A (hybrid reserved + burst). Cost delta needs quantification but should let us keep the public launch date.
- Quantization: amber -> temporary 8-bit fallback for canary; full fix ~10 business days.
- Docs/runbook: Ben, need the rollback + billing verification steps final by Wednesday COB.

Concrete asks (action owners):
- Laura: confirm ProcureSync partial contract approval and provide final wording for the slide by Wed 18:00 PT.
- Marissa: quantify expected cost delta for Option A and confirm the 3-day QA gating timeline by Wed 12:00 PT. Attach the go-no-go CSV with the engineering recommendation.
- Ben: upload release-runbook v1 to the Drive folder and confirm canary rollback steps by Wed 17:00 PT.

Decision guidance for the execs at QBR (what I'll present):
- Recommend go for public launch if: (a) ProcureSync partial is approved, (b) Option A reserved+burst secured, and (c) 8-bit fallback gated for canary with automated QA checks.
- Recommend delay if any of the above is not confirmed by Wed EOD — we will present the contingency plan and revised dates.

I'll create the single-slide decision view and circulate for a final sanity check on Thursday morning. Please mark the attached go-no-go-matrix.csv with Yes/No and rationale.

Markus
VP Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: release-readiness-checklist.pdf, launch-dependencies.csv, go-no-go-matrix.csv
